source.title: Vanishing Curvature and the Power of Adaptive Methods in Randomly Initialized Deep Networks
source.authors: Antonio Orvieto; Jonas Köhler; Dario Pavllo; T. Hofmann; Aurélien Lucchi

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present; some plotted results are available only as figures, without extractable numeric values.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares optimizers on held-out accuracy and reports an overfitting result for RMSprop, using its own deep-network experiments rather than the optimizer comparisons in the claim’s cited studies.
record.gate_note: The study reports optimizer comparisons for training and test accuracy, but most test-accuracy values are figure-only. These results do not test random-label memorization, width sweeps for test error, convolutional versus fully connected generalization, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples. Initialization-gradient and Hessian measurements are not rows because they do not measure the claimed training–test generalization gap.
record.test_reason: Figure 10 compares adaptive optimizers with SGD on held-out image-classification accuracy in unusually deep networks, bearing on V4 in a new architectural setting. Learning rates were grid-searched for training accuracy. The supplied text does not preserve readable curve values or explicitly establish the held-out optimizer ranking.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors connect vanishing gradients with vanishing curvature at initialization and argue that adaptive methods can escape the resulting flat plateaus. They separately report heavy RMSprop overfitting on the unregularized stripped ResNet; they do not explicitly conclude that its held-out performance is worse than SGD's.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes and compares optimizer behavior in randomly initialized deep networks, focusing on initialization curvature and optimization; it does not reproduce the optimizer generalization comparisons described in V4.
record.method_sensitivity: Network width and depth, initialization, architecture, and optimizer affect gradient and curvature behavior; the paper also reports overfitting for RMSprop on the unregularized stripped ResNet.

fits_no_version.finding: RMSprop heavily overfits the unregularized 500-layer stripped ResNet on CIFAR-10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A very deep convolutional network trained successfully with RMSprop can exhibit a substantial training–test gap without regularization.

fits_no_version.finding: Adaptive methods escape flat initialization plateaus and train deep networks that SGD struggles to optimize.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Curvature adaptation can improve optimization in deep randomly initialized networks with vanishing gradients and curvature.

record.problems: Held-out accuracy comparisons are shown as figures without textual values or pairwise conclusions. The explicit overfitting statement concerns one large unregularized architecture and does not establish a general adaptive-optimizer gap.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for the same optimizer and model’s training accuracy: those do not independently measure held-out generalization. Initialization-only gradient and Hessian magnitude plots are outside the versions’ named measures.

untested.parts: Fixed random-label fitting versus natural-label and random-label held-out accuracy.
Test error across widths beyond the width required for zero training error; the width experiments principally concern initialization and trainability.
Comparative held-out performance of convolutional and fully connected networks, including learned locality and transferred initialization.

Language benchmarks, broader hyperparameter tuning, decoupled weight decay, switching optimizers, and comparisons at similarly successful training performance. The study uses learning-rate selection by training accuracy and no learning-rate scheduling for the stripped ResNet.
Batch-size interventions under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove large-batch penalties.
Dropout interventions and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance at trained solutions and its association with generalization gaps; initialization Hessians do not measure this.
Removal of highly memorized examples versus random removal and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the extracted limits_scope verdict: V4 already predicts possible adaptive-method generalization disadvantages, and overfitting alone establishes no comparative disadvantage. No directional verdict is justified by the supplied text. Figure 10 contains relevant comparisons, but its curves are not recoverable from this text extraction. Training-accuracy results were explicitly declared in rows_left_out, so they are not missing rows.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization compared with natural-label generalization.
Test error as width increases beyond the interpolation threshold.
Generalization comparison between convolutional and fully connected networks.
The study does not test the cited image-classification and language benchmarks, broader hyperparameter tuning, decoupled weight decay, switching from Adam to SGD, or word-level language models.
Large-batch comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removal of memorized training examples and retraining.
